whatChanged: ADVANCED: Nvidia signed a definitive agreement on 2 September to buy Hugging Face for about $12.93bn -- roughly $11.9bn to stockholders plus up to $1.0bn of employee retention equity -- and confirmed it publicly the next day, with closing guided to the first half of 2027 (rumored → confirmed) (nvda-huggingface-acquisition)

ADVANCED: Aurora Cannabis' board, on the unanimous recommendation of its special committee and a TD Securities opinion, formally told shareholders to reject Curaleaf's hostile bid and to withdraw any shares already tendered (confirmed → confirmed) (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid)

NEW: SoundHound AI's takeover of LivePerson cleared its last condition as LivePerson stockholders approved 0.4673 SoundHound shares plus $3.31 cash per share by roughly 6.34m votes to 134k, with closing set for 4 September (soun-liveperson-acquisition)

NEW: Diversified Energy agreed to buy Birch Permian Holdings for $1.8bn, the largest deal in its 25-year history, adding ~68,000 boe/d and lifting group production ~35% and adjusted EBITDA ~55%, alongside a Carlyle acquisition framework widened from $2bn to up to $10bn (dec-birch-permian-acquisition)

NEW: Advent International, already Definitive Healthcare's controlling owner, put a non-binding $1.02-a-share all-cash going-private proposal to a special committee of independent directors for the stock it and founder Jason Krantz do not hold (dh-advent-take-private)

NEW: Samsung Life is reported to be negotiating a ~15% stake in Principal Financial Group for $3.6-4.4bn, enough to displace Vanguard as PFG's largest shareholder (samsung-life-principal-financial-stake)

NEW: Samsung Fire & Marine is reported to be negotiating the buyout of the ~60% of Lloyd's specialty insurer Canopius it does not already own, the general-insurance half of a paired ~$6.6bn Samsung push overseas (samsung-fire-canopius-buyout)

NEW: Vertex completed its roughly $10bn, $85-a-share cash acquisition of Crinetics Pharmaceuticals, its largest deal, taking ownership of acromegaly drug Palsonify and an endocrine-disease pipeline (vrtx-crinetics-acquisition)

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsor-, sovereign-, cooperative- and strategic-led buyouts keep pulling listed names off public markets, and London is now the densest single hunting ground: a single day this month took UK takeover activity past $100bn for the year, with Veritas Capital agreeing 940p a share for Bodycote after outbidding CVC in an auction that also drew Apollo (boy-veritas-take-private) and Epiris agreeing 1,120p for Gamma Communications at a 53% premium (gama-epiris-take-private) -- both profitable mid-caps that public markets rated a third or more below what private capital would pay. Elsewhere the contested approaches remain open and unresolved: Uber's BaFin-approved offer document opened a EUR41.50-a-share, ~EUR13bn cash tender for Delivery Hero running to 5 November with only a 50%-plus-one minimum (dher-uber-takeover-offer); Couche-Tard's PLN 32.00-a-share tender for Zabka is open to 25 September with 57% locked up by irrevocables (zab-couchetard-tender-offer); Curaleaf's hostile tender for Aurora Cannabis runs to 1 December against a special committee still telling holders to take no action (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid); KKR has an unsolicited ~$9bn, $42.50-a-share approach on the table for UGI with no board response yet (ugi-kkr-takeover-bid); WSP Global will file an offer memorandum with the Dutch AFM by 15 October to press a twice-rejected EUR51.50-a-share bid for Arcadis (arcad-wsp-takeover-bid); Abu Dhabi's L'IMAD is offering Dh6.25 a share for the ~24.6% of AD Ports it does not hold (adports-limad-takeover-bid); and JBS has proposed taking in the ~18% of Pilgrim's Pride it does not own at 2.086 JBS shares apiece (ppc-jbs-minority-buyout). Where two bidders show up the auction, not the opening offer, sets the exit -- DNO's $5.214 a share for Capricorn Energy topped Genel's recommended bid by about 10% and flipped the board (cne-dno-acquisition), and Coricelli's EUR500m won exclusivity over Deoleo after a 31 August ultimatum, leaving Dcoop's EUR470m passed over but not withdrawn (ole-coricelli-takeover-bid, ole-dcoop-takeover-bid). Against all that, two approaches died on price rather than on regulators: Trian shelved its Wendy's take-private (wen-trian-takeover-bid), and Advent and Stripe walked from a $60.50-a-share, ~$53bn bid for PayPal after a 40% run squeezed the premium out of it (pypl-stripe-advent-takeover-bid). At the finished end, Two Harbors' $12.00-a-share sale to CrossCountry Mortgage has closed (two-crosscountry-acquisition), while Francisco Partners' $650m for Weave is signed and waiting on approvals (weav-francisco-partners-take-private). The newest approach is also the smallest and the most conflicted: Advent International, already Definitive Healthcare's controlling owner, has put a non-binding $1.02-a-share all-cash proposal to a special committee of independent directors for the Class A stock and TopCo interests it and founder Jason Krantz do not hold, which makes the committee, not the premium, the only thing standing between minority holders and a take-under (dh-advent-take-private).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital keeps pouring into the physical layer of AI compute, and the commitments run years ahead of the workloads: AWS has agreed to deploy 2 million additional Nvidia GPUs across its global footprint in 2027-2028, tripling the 1-million programme announced in March and adding Vera CPU infrastructure, custom-HBM NVLink Fusion and a 100,000-GPU US government AI factory (amzn-nvidia-gpu-expansion). The bottleneck keeps moving down the stack to the unglamorous physical inputs, and buyers are paying up for them. Getting power onto a site is now the scarcest of those inputs, and this week Vertiv paid for it directly: $1.45bn in cash plus up to $1.15bn of earnout for UtilityInnovation Group's microgrid controls, on-site generation orchestration and behind-the-meter architecture, explicitly framed as shortening time-to-power for customers who can build a data center faster than a utility can energise it (vrt-utilityinnovation-acquisition). Cooling is the same trade one component over: SLB is spending $4.1bn including assumed debt on Kelvion's cooling and heat-exchange technology to underwrite a data-center business it targets at $4.5-5bn of revenue and $700-800m of adjusted EBITDA in 2028 (slb-kelvion-acquisition), and Madison Air is paying $5.4bn for ebm-papst's fans and motor systems partly for the same opportunity (mair-ebmpapst-acquisition). The pull now reaches the regulated utilities themselves -- KKR's unsolicited ~$9bn approach for UGI's gas and electric utility, midstream and propane franchise is explicitly framed against data-center load growth (ugi-kkr-takeover-bid) -- and upstream into gas supply, where SOCAR is paying Comstock $1.65bn for working interests in the Haynesville, the basin feeding Gulf Coast LNG and the power demand behind it (crk-socar-haynesville-partnership). The Ohio megaproject remains the clearest single example: Nvidia's backstop for OpenAI's PORTS-Pike campus is firm at up to $105bn of credit for the first 4.25GW, with an option covering a further 3.75GW (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), and Nvidia has separately put $1.5bn of equity into developer SB Energy, which with SoftBank plans at least 10GW of new generation, a 9.2GW on-site gas plant costing ~$33bn and $4.2bn of Ohio grid investment (nvda-sbenergy-investment). Elsewhere Core Scientific paid ~$444m to take ~440MW of in-service, grid-connected Oklahoma capacity off a rival miner (corz-polaris-acquisition), while Broadcom is sounding lenders for more than $60bn against a chip-leasing vehicle aimed at over 20GW of frontier-lab compute by 2028 (avgo-anthropic-chip-financing). At the silicon layer Marvell has locked Google into a multi-year custom-chip programme for the TPU ecosystem (mrvl-google-tpu-partnership) and Micron is committing $10bn over a decade to a Boise foundational-research hub (mu-research-labs-investment), while SK hynix returns a record KRW40trn of the HBM windfall to shareholders rather than adding another leg of capacity (skhynix-buyback-cancellation-2026).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep being resolved by judges, regulators and shareholder ballots, in both directions. Paramount Skydance has satisfied every regulatory condition in its Warner Bros. Discovery merger agreement, yet still cannot close until five days after a 12-day antitrust trial set for 2 March 2027 -- and the negotiated way out has broken down, with California AG Rob Bonta cancelling the settlement meeting and leaving the $1.88bn bond demand due 30 September and the ~$7m-a-day ticking fee running from 1 October as the live pressure points (psky-wbd-acquisition). Western Union's Intermex deal cleared New York's DFS on 14 August only for California's DFPI to suspend its own approval extension the day before, and the parties say they will close promptly once the DFPI reinstates it (imxi-westernunion-acquisition). Uber's open tender for Delivery Hero shows how long the tail can be even on an agreed deal: merger-control and financial-regulatory clearances across a 99-country footprint push guided settlement out to the second half of 2027 (dher-uber-takeover-offer). Politics is now doing the same work as regulation in the Deoleo auction, where the Spanish agriculture ministry has openly argued the world's largest olive-oil bottler should end up with a domestic buyer even as the board hands exclusivity to Italy's Coricelli (ole-coricelli-takeover-bid). Gates keep opening as well: Real's arrangement with RE/MAX cleared the Supreme Court of British Columbia and closed on 24 August with Real REMAX Group trading on Nasdaq from the 25th (reax-remax-combination), Deutz's extraordinary general meeting backed the capital increase behind its EUR1.6bn FFG purchase with 99.7% in favour after an unconditional Bundeskartellamt clearance (dez-ffg-acquisition), and California's PUC signed off on Charter-Cox as the final clearance needed, letting a $34.5bn merger close fifteen months after it was struck (chtr-cox-acquisition). The shareholder ballot did the same work at the smaller end of the market this week, in the deals' favour: LivePerson holders approved SoundHound's takeover by roughly 6.34m votes to 134k after an adjourned August meeting, clearing the last condition and setting closing for 4 September (soun-liveperson-acquisition), and Vertex closed its ~$10bn purchase of Crinetics on 1 September once regulatory clearances and the target's shareholder vote were in (vrtx-crinetics-acquisition).

themes.label: Chipmakers funding or locking in the customers that buy their chips
themes.note: Vendor financing, equity and exclusivity remain the standard shape of frontier-AI deals, and the entanglement now runs in every direction at once. Nvidia's OpenAI backstop is a firm commitment of up to $105bn against the first 4.25GW of the Ohio campus (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), and alongside it Nvidia has taken a $1.5bn equity stake in campus developer SB Energy that makes it the sole supplier of compute on the site it is financing (nvda-sbenergy-investment) -- the circularity critics object to, written into the cap table. It extends past financing into capability: Nvidia paid Poolside $6bn to license the 'Model Factory' training stack behind its Laguna models, put $1bn of equity into the startup and hired the 109 engineers who built it (nvda-poolside-model-factory-license), and its purchase of Hugging Face -- the distribution point where developers pull the open-source models they then have to run on Nvidia silicon -- is now signed and public at about $12.93bn, roughly $11.9bn to stockholders plus up to $1.0bn of retention equity, with Nvidia promising the platform stays open and its own compute stays optional (nvda-huggingface-acquisition). The newest version of the trade points at the competitive threat rather than the customer: $3.5bn of convertible bonds into MediaTek, in exchange for MediaTek building the custom accelerators hyperscalers commission to avoid Nvidia GPUs on top of Nvidia's own NVLink Fusion interconnect (nvda-mediatek-nvlink-investment). The straightforward version still runs alongside all of it: AWS has committed to 2 million more Nvidia GPUs in 2027-2028 despite designing its own accelerators (amzn-nvidia-gpu-expansion). Broadcom has taken the financing trade further than anyone, seeking more than $60bn of debt for a vehicle that buys Broadcom's own custom chips and leases them to Anthropic and potentially OpenAI, with Broadcom guaranteeing part of the senior tranche (avgo-anthropic-chip-financing). Marvell has inverted the trade entirely, handing Google a warrant over up to $12.2bn of its own stock -- vesting only as Google buys chips -- so the customer ends up owning the supplier (mrvl-google-tpu-partnership).

themes.label: Financial firms buying platforms and product lines rather than building them
themes.note: Listed financial companies keep concluding that the capabilities the market now pays for are quicker to buy than to build, and that what they are buying is a fee stream or a distribution platform rather than plain assets. The largest is Aon's $17bn purchase of USI from KKR, funded entirely with new debt, to assemble a US middle-market broking platform against $395m of targeted run-rate synergies -- distribution into the segment where organic growth holds up best, bought rather than grown (aon-usi-acquisition). Victory Capital is paying about $7bn -- $4bn cash, $2bn in new shares and $575m of assumed notes -- for First Eagle Investments, taking combined assets to roughly $571bn and acquiring First Eagle's $41bn CLO and alternative-credit platform to serve as the enlarged group's alternatives arm (vctr-first-eagle-acquisition). At the small end, Velocity Financial is paying only $63m for KKR-backed Toorak's operating platform but taking on management of the ~$3bn loan portfolio sold alongside it, converting a balance-sheet lender into one that also earns fees on third-party capital (vel-toorak-platform-acquisition). In each case the target is a fee-rate-defensible platform rather than AUM, and the buyer faces compression in its own core business. The pattern has now gone cross-border and into insurance: Samsung Life is reported to be negotiating a ~15% stake in Principal Financial Group for $3.6-4.4bn, enough to displace Vanguard as its largest holder (samsung-life-principal-financial-stake), while Samsung Fire & Marine negotiates the ~60% of Lloyd's specialty insurer Canopius it does not already own (samsung-fire-canopius-buyout) -- a US retirement distribution platform and a Lloyd's underwriting licence bought rather than built at home, in what would together be the largest cross-border acquisition a Korean financial group has done.
